hints: Look at this as a Hess cycle puzzle, your target product $\text{C}_2\text{H}_2$ is a reactant in one of the data reactions.
Keep the first reaction as it is to give you $2\text{C(s)}$, but reverse the second reaction so $\text{C}_2\text{H}_4$ cancels and $\text{C}_2\text{H}_2$ is formed.
Remember to change the sign when you reverse a reaction, then add the two $\Delta H$ values together to find X.
walkthrough:
**Write down what you want**

You want to make $\text{C}_2\text{H}_2$ from $2\text{C(s)} + \text{H}_2\text{(g)}$. Look at where those species appear in the data.

$$\text{Target: } 2\text{C(s)} + \text{H}_2\text{(g)} \rightarrow \text{C}_2\text{H}_2\text{(g)}$$

**Arrange the data reactions using Hess's Law**

Keep reaction 1 as written because it already has $2\text{C(s)}$ as a reactant. Reverse reaction 2 so $\text{C}_2\text{H}_2$ becomes a product and $\text{C}_2\text{H}_4$ cancels.

$$\text{(1): } 2\text{C} + 2\text{H}_2 \rightarrow \text{C}_2\text{H}_4 \quad \Delta H = +52.2$$
$$\text{(2) reversed: } \text{C}_2\text{H}_4 \rightarrow \text{C}_2\text{H}_2 + \text{H}_2 \quad \Delta H = +175.8$$

**Add the equations and the enthalpy changes**

Adding (1) + reversed (2), the $\text{C}_2\text{H}_4$ and one $\text{H}_2$ cancel to leave exactly the target equation. Add the $\Delta H$ values, remembering the sign flip.

$$X = (+52.2) + (+175.8) = +228.0 \text{ kJ mol}^{-1}$$

options.A: Incorrect. This is $ -175.8 - 52.2 = -228.0$. You get this if you do (reaction 2) minus (reaction 1) instead of (reaction 1) minus (reaction 2). That builds the reverse of the target reaction.
options.B: Incorrect. This is $+52.2 + (-175.8) = -123.6$. You get this if you add the reactions without reversing the second one. You must reverse it to turn $\text{C}_2\text{H}_2$ from a reactant into a product, which changes $-175.8$ to $+175.8$.
options.C: Incorrect. This is $+175.8 - 52.2 = +123.6$. You get this if you reverse the wrong reaction. The first reaction already has $2\text{C(s)}$ in the correct place, it is the second reaction that must be reversed.
options.D: Correct. By Hess's Law, X = (reaction 1) - (reaction 2) = +52.2 - (-175.8) = +228.0 kJ mol-1. Reversing the hydrogenation of ethyne makes it endothermic, and adding it to the formation of ethene gives the formation of ethyne.
